app.title: MammaScope · IHC vs MammaTyper® concordance analysis
app.summary: A person uploads one or more immunohistochemistry spreadsheet exports and one or more RT-qPCR report PDFs, then runs a seven-step pipeline. The pipeline checks both formats, pulls biomarker results out of each source, pairs records by biopsy number and stores the matched samples in a database. It sets aside the records found in only one source. The results screen shows batch counts and automatic alerts for each sample, with the reasons grouped by priority. It also has a heatmap of agreement for each sample and biomarker, and the combined table. From there the person downloads a table, a concordance workbook with a dashboard, and a clinical PDF report for each sample. Separate modes let them query the stored samples, review and delete the unmatched records, and compute agreement statistics across every sample collected so far.

task.text: Check two diagnostic methods against each other for the same samples: flag the samples where they disagree for review, and measure how well the methods agree overall.

data.text: Paired results from two assays on the same biopsies: categorical scores pulled from the free-text reports of one method, and quantitative expression values with fixed cutoffs from the other, joined on a shared sample id and kept in a growing database.
data.item: a biopsy sample with four biomarker results from each of the two methods

stage.text: comparing a molecular assay's results with routine staining after both reports exist, before clinical review and reporting

mechanism.text: A stepped flow (upload, process, results) gates each stage on the one before, and a progress bar tracks the pipeline. The results screen puts summary metrics, per-sample alert lists, an agreement heatmap with hover detail and a table colour-coded by data source above a set of export buttons. Other modes in the sidebar open database queries with up to three combined filters, a review of unmatched records with delete-by-id, and a statistics dashboard.

field.text: method concordance between immunohistochemistry and RT-qPCR biomarker testing in breast cancer pathology

workflow.name: match records from two sources and measure where they agree

steps.here: Two uploaders, one for spreadsheet exports and one for report PDFs, each accept several files and merge them. 'Ir al paso 2' appears only when both sources are loaded.

steps.step: pair the records from both sources by a shared id
steps.here: 'Procesar y guardar muestras en BD' runs seven steps with a progress bar: validate both formats, extract the records, sort out repeated biopsy ids by tissue block, fuse on sample_id, log unmatched ids from either side, and save the fused samples.

steps.step: flag the items that need attention, with reasons
steps.here: Automatic alerts for each sample are grouped by priority (discordances, possible discordances, HER2 completeness, values near a cutoff, missing data), each with summary chips. An expander lists the ids that appear in only one file.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A heatmap with samples as rows and the four biomarkers plus a global column marks each cell OK, DISC or missing. Hovering a cell shows both methods' raw values, and totals of concordant, discordant and incomplete samples sit below.

Downloads include a CSV of the batch, an Excel table with headers coloured by source, a concordance workbook with a dashboard sheet, and PDF reports for the whole batch (as a ZIP or one merged file) or for one selected sample.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: The stored samples, and separately the unmatched records, can be loaded in full or narrowed with up to three column filters ('contiene' or exact value). Unmatched records that have been resolved can be deleted by id.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For every sample collected so far, each biomarker gets percent agreement, Cohen's kappa with a 95% CI, McNemar's test, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and diagnostic OR. These come with confusion-matrix heatmaps, a kappa interval chart, a radar profile, charts of which way the discordances run, and plain-language verdicts.

distinctive: Biomarker values are pulled from the free-text clinical reports of one source and from PDF pages of the other, so validation and sorting out repeated ids by tissue block come before matching
Each quantitative value is placed in a category by configurable cutoffs for each gene, and values within a small distance of a cutoff raise critical or near-cutoff alerts
Records found in only one source are kept in their own table for follow-up and deleted once resolved, so pairing gaps are tracked rather than silently dropped
Agreement is measured as a diagnostic-test comparison (kappa, McNemar, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV) over the growing database, not only within one batch
A clinical PDF report is generated for each sample, showing where each value falls against its cutoffs
